summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his detailed study of the book of purification (Al-Wajiz), focusing on the comprehensive description of ghusl (full ritual bathing). He explains the Prophet Muhammad's typical method of performing ghusl, which begins with washing the hands, followed by cleansing the private parts, performing wudu as done before prayer, working water through the hair roots, pouring water three times over the head, washing both sides of the body, and finally washing the feet. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that this detailed narration is considered the most reliable and comprehensive description found in the six canonical hadith collections. He also discusses the distinction between the Prophet's usual method of ghusl and his minimal approach when ill or bedridden, and explains why he left the feet for last in his typical practice.
